The absorbing screen uses a third-order fractal Hilbert curve metal strip array combined with a CVD graphene sheet.
Graphene's surface conductivity is tunable by changing chemical potential via external voltage.
At 0 eV chemical potential, the absorption bandwidth is from 8.9 GHz to 18.1 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 68.1%.
The central frequency of absorption can be tuned from 13.5 GHz to 19.0 GHz as chemical potential varies from 0 to 0.4 eV.
The total thickness of the absorbing screen is approximately 3.4 mm, close to the theoretical minimum thickness of 3.1 mm for nonmagnetic absorbers.
Graphene's surface impedance ranges from about 1.2 kΩ at 0 eV to 110 Ω at 0.4 eV chemical potential.
The Hilbert curve metal strip array provides multiple narrowband resonances enabling wideband impedance matching.
Dielectric layers D1 and D2 have thicknesses of 1.2 mm and 2.2 mm respectively with dielectric constant εr=4.3.
The metal strips are made of copper with conductivity 5.96×10^7 S/m and thickness 5 μm.
Graphene sheet is placed directly underneath the metal strips to enhance power dissipation via strong electric field interaction.
The chemical potential of graphene is controlled by applying DC voltage between metal strips and an underlying polysilicon layer separated by a silicon dioxide layer.
The absorption at 0 eV chemical potential achieves above 90% over a 9.2 GHz bandwidth.
Without graphene, the absorber shows narrowband absorption peaks with poor broadband performance.
Dielectric losses have minimal effect on absorption performance; graphene is the main absorbing element.
The design achieves broadband impedance matching due to graphene's nearly frequency-independent surface impedance in the microwave band.
The carrier density in graphene is modulated by the applied voltage and dielectric thickness, affecting chemical potential.
The device is grounded with a perfect electric conductor (PEC) to eliminate transmission.
The fractal Hilbert curve structure is chosen for its multi-resonance properties and compact footprint.
The absorber's thickness corresponds to about 0.15 wavelengths at the central frequency of 13.5 GHz.
The fabrication involves sputtering polysilicon and silicon dioxide layers, transferring graphene, patterning metal strips by e-beam lithography, and bonding dielectric layers.
